title: Mother and son again, 1861
hook: after long years apart, Duleep meets his mother, and she tells him of his heritage
carry: she told him who he was

segments.voice: Yesterday, Elveden, and your line was far from punjab. Where did your mind go when you asked where you belong? Today, someone arrives who remembers. Day nine hundred forty-three.

What do you say to a mother you last saw when you were small? A hotel in Calcutta. A grown man in English clothes waits in a room. The door opens, and a woman comes in, older than he remembers, her eyesight failing. She is Maharani Jind Kaur, the queen who was sent away. When she reaches him, the story goes, she runs her hands over his head, looking for his uncut hair, and finds it cut short. Today: mother and son again.
screen: `A HOTEL IN CALCUTTA.` → `A QUEEN WHOSE EYES ARE FAILING.` → `HER HANDS ON HIS HEAD.`

segments.voice: First, where she had been. After she was separated from her son and sent away, Jind Kaur was held as a prisoner. She escaped, in disguise, and made her way to Nepal, where she lived in exile under the protection of its rulers. All those years, letters between mother and son were watched or stopped. Second, the meeting. Duleep Singh asked to see her, and in time the British allowed it, as long as she did not go back to the Punjab. They met in Calcutta. The boy she had last held was now a grown man, a Christian, living as an English gentleman. Third, what she told him. Jind Kaur came with him to England and lived near him in London. She talked to him about the Punjab, about his father, Ranjit Singh, about the kingdom and how it was lost, and about the Sikh faith he had been raised away from. Histories that follow his life mark this as the moment something in him began to turn. Fourth, a mother's blessing in the Guru Granth Sahib. There's a hymn of Guru Arjan in which a mother speaks to her son: this is your mother's blessing, son, that you never forget the Lord for even an instant. The blessing is about remembering the Lord. In Calcutta, and then in London, this mother's gift was a remembering too: she gave her son back the story of who he was. That's today's line.
screen: `AN ESCAPE TO NEPAL.` · `A MEETING IN CALCUTTA.` · `STORIES OF THE PUNJAB.` · `A MOTHER'S BLESSING.` · then, large: `SHE TOLD HIM WHO HE WAS.`

segments.voice: Two minutes with an elder. Sit, and let your breath slow. Bring to mind your mother, or a grandparent, or any elder who knew you when you were small. Picture their face, their hands, the sound of their voice. What did they tell you about where you come from? If they're living, think of one question you'd like to ask them. If they've died, think of one thing they told you that you'd like to keep. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Asees, blessing, a mother's blessing to her son never to forget the Lord: Jind Kaur and Duleep Singh, meeting in Calcutta after long years apart. Today's word.
Your line: she told him who he was. Today, call your mother or an elder, and ask them one thing about where you come from. Day nine hundred forty-three.

howItsDone: Sikhs honor Maharani Jind Kaur as a mother who never stopped resisting the loss of her son and her kingdom, and the meeting in Calcutta is told as the moment Duleep Singh began to recover his heritage.

notes: No year or span of years in the voice (the index title gives 1861; outline says thirteen years); confirm before adding.
The hands-on-his-head, looking for uncut hair detail is a widely told story; confirm the source.
The meeting at a Calcutta hotel (Spence's Hotel) and the condition that she not stay in the Punjab: confirm.
Editor: 'would not stay in the Punjab' changed to 'did not go back to the Punjab' (she was in Nepal, not the Punjab, before the meeting), in the teach and the myth item.
Guru Arjan's hymn (poota maataa kee asees...) paraphrased; confirm Ang 496 and Gurmukhi ਅਸੀਸ.
Audit: the teach no longer equates the hymn's blessing (remembering the Lord) with Jind Kaur telling her son his history; it now draws the link without claiming they are the same.
